title: Open Science and the Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Exchange
what_changed: The report evaluates how generative AI could either strengthen accessibility, multilingual exchange, and discoverability or undermine Open Science through obscured provenance, infrastructure dependency, unequal capabilities, and "synthetic overload": more generated content than researchers and systems can reliably verify.
why_it_matters: Its policy options treat scientific exchange as public-interest infrastructure. Openness is reformulated as a combination of accessibility, provenance, reproducibility, inclusion, skills, and institutional capacity, not merely unrestricted availability. It provides a timely European policy vocabulary connecting Open Science, AI-mediated publishing, research integrity, and infrastructure governance.
